title: Karna ne apna divya kavach kyun ukhada?
hooks: Karna ne apna divya kavach ukhad diya...
Divya kavach wala Karna ne kyun chhoda apna suraksha kavach?
Kya aap apni divya taqat daan kar sakte ho?
hook_why: Mystery-tease hook shows the shocking act immediately, first sentence incomplete to force retention past 3 seconds, visual of golden armor tearing away creates instant curiosity.
metaphor: Golden armor cracking open to reveal an inner light that never fades — invincibility was a cage, generosity the key that freed his true identity.

cast.Karna: Tall, broad-shouldered warrior with golden skin, wearing ornate golden armor (kavach) and large golden earrings (kundal), long hair tied in a bun, calm determined expression, traditional dhoti, radiant but mortal.
cast.Indra_brahmin: Old brahmin with white beard, simple cotton dhoti, wooden staff, kamandalu, humble posture, but eyes sharp and divine.
cast.Indra_true: Four-armed deity riding white elephant Airavata, golden crown, lightning in hand, majestic, surrounded by celestial glow.

caption:
Karna ne apni divya taqat khud hi chhor di. Kyun?
Mahabharata Vana Parva ki yeh kahaani batati hai ki asli pehchaan daan mein hoti hai, kavach mein nahi.

claims.claim: Karna tore off his divine armor (kavach) and earrings (kundal) when Indra asked for them in disguise.
claims.basis: Mahabharata, Vana Parva (Araneya Parva), chapters 29-30: Indra approaches Karna as a brahmin during his sun worship; Karna recognizes him but gives the armor and earrings anyway.

claims.claim: The armor and earrings were part of Karna's body, making him invincible; removing them made him mortal.
claims.basis: Mahabharata, Vana Parva: The kavach and kundal were born with Karna, attached to his flesh; their removal caused bleeding and loss of immortality.

claims.claim: Indra rewarded Karna's generosity with the Shakti astra (weapon).
claims.basis: Mahabharata, Vana Parva: After receiving the armor, Indra reveals his true form and grants Karna the infallible Shakti weapon.
Standard scholarly reference for this episode; the story appears in the Araneya Parva section of Vana Parva.
